name: cutaway_grammar
why: What a cut of the cutaway reference style may say about itself, as rows: each field of the cuts layer (studio2/cuts.py) names the values it takes and the reference item it is read against. The numbers are never written here: they are read from the reference library (studio.patterns.reading) whenever the grammar is shown or checked. A new kind of opening, motion, change or graphic is a row.

opens.means: how the cut shows what is hidden inside the thing

section_cut.means: cut open in section: a clean slice with the cut face toward the camera
section_cut.prompt: cut open in a clean section, as if a giant knife sliced it, the sliced faces of walls and slabs visible as clean grey cut edges

transparency.means: an outer skin made see-through over what it holds
transparency.prompt: its outer skin rendered see-through glass-like so what it holds shows inside

explode.means: its parts pulled apart along their axis
explode.prompt: its parts pulled apart along one axis with even gaps, each part whole

real_to_diagram.means: the real thing beside or turning into its diagram
real_to_diagram.prompt: the real thing beside a clean simplified model of itself

none.means: nothing is opened: the thing is seen whole, or the cut before already opened it

camera.move.means: the camera over the cut: held, pushed in or pulled back

still.means: held: what changes is the scene

push.means: a slow push in toward what the cut is about

pull.means: a slow pull back to show what holds it

camera.amount.means: how much the picture grows (push) or shrinks (pull) over the cut, as a share of its size

change.kind.means: what changes on screen over the cut

move.means: something moves along a path (water, a speck, a box on a rail)

state.means: something becomes another state (lit to dark, empty to full); the last picture is the first with only that changed

none.means: nothing changes but the camera and the drawn flow

level.prompt: seen at eye level, straight on

scale_step.means: the step from the cut before: the reel goes from the place to its part and back

graphics.means: what is drawn over the picture (never painted into it)

label.means: a word or two naming a part, beside it with a thin leader

path_trace.means: a flow or a route drawn as glowing colour along its way

subtitle.means: where the subtitle sits and how long its line is

label_text.means: the height of a label's letters, as a share of the frame height

scales.means: how big what fills the frame is, widest first: a cut's scale_step follows from its scale and the cut before's

colours.means: what a drawn colour stands for (the reference draws a flow or a path as colour)

red.means: a route, a boundary, a failure

orange.means: dust, heat, a small thing to follow

white.means: a neutral path or a pointer
